skill.name: un-editorial-check
skill.description: Review English user-visible copy against documented United Nations editorial rules, with separate human review for claims, harmful language, and diplomatic wording.
skill.summary: Review English copy with source-linked editorial findings and separate human review for claims and sensitive wording.
skill.author: ahaomar

security_audit.summary: Of 400 supplied findings, 394 are false positives; six confirm unsafe baseline creation or blocking special-file reads, with additional PDF denial-of-service risk. No evidence found of prompt injection or intentional data exfiltration in reviewed context. Review was capped at 400 of 5,037 matches; the remaining 4,637 require manual review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 400/5037 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 4637 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: PDF decompression and parsing lack practical resource budgets.
remediation.suggestion: Limit input and cumulative decoded bytes, validate predictor dimensions, and run parsing in an isolated worker with a deadline and memory limit.

remediation.issue: Baseline and claim-register readers can block on attacker-controlled special files.
remediation.suggestion: Open nonblocking descriptors, verify regular-file type with fstat, and enforce byte limits before reading baseline and claim-register contents. Add regression tests for FIFO inputs.

remediation.issue: Baseline creation follows dangling symbolic links after a missing-file read.
remediation.suggestion: Create baseline files exclusively with no-follow protection, validate descriptor identity, and reject symbolic links before writing. Test dangling links and concurrent destination replacement.

remediation.issue: Static review covers only 400 of 5,037 reported matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual adjudication of the remaining 4,637 matches before automatic publication; keep the incomplete-coverage publication guard active.

content.user_title: Review Copy Against UN Editorial Rules
content.value_statement: Editorial inconsistencies and sensitive wording are difficult to track across documents and websites. This skill checks extracted English copy and separates rule violations from human review.
actual_capabilities: Extract user-visible copy from HTML, Markdown, plain text, supported JavaScript literals, PDFs, and Word or OpenDocument body text.
Check documented spelling, terminology, grammar, date, numeral, and register rules with source-linked findings.
Separate deterministic violations, editorial heuristics, harmful-language review, diplomatic sensitivity, and optional audits.
Generate terminal, JSON, SARIF, PDF, and self-contained HTML reports.
Preview deterministic corrections and apply approved changes only to eligible regular Markdown and plain-text files.
Support organization profiles, house glossaries, claim registers, baseline comparisons, and explicit URL retrieval.
limitations: Rules target English copy and do not verify facts, provide legal advice, or certify United Nations compliance.
PDF extraction provides no OCR and refuses encrypted, image-only, or unrecoverable documents. PDFs cannot receive applied fixes; hostile PDFs can exhaust resources.
Word and OpenDocument extraction excludes headers, footers, text boxes, footnotes, endnotes, and comments.
Optional audits and glossary findings do not affect exit codes. Explicit URL retrieval follows redirects and requires trusted destinations.

use_cases.description: Check briefing papers for spelling, dates, terminology, and sensitive wording while preserving source references for editorial decisions.

use_cases.title: Check Product Interface Copy
use_cases.description: Review visible HTML and supported JavaScript copy before release, with optional publishing or accessibility findings reported separately.

use_cases.title: Track Evidence Review
use_cases.description: Create a claim register for detected figures and comparisons, then check source and reference-date completeness after human review.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [draft.md] with un-editorial-check. Report deterministic violations separately from findings requiring human review. Do not modify the file.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Editorial Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [document.pdf] and write an HTML review report to [report.html]. Preserve rule sources and PDF page references. State extraction refusals clearly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Document review with a shareable report

prompt_templates.title: Preview Approved Corrections
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the target files in [content-directory]. Preview deterministic fixes for eligible prose files. Request approval before applying changes, then review the resulting diff.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Evidence and Baseline Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [content-directory] using [organization-profile.json] and [claims.json]. Compare [baseline.json] and export SARIF. Keep optional audit findings separate from editorial failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review in an existing CI workflow

output: The checker reports the matching rule and source. The draft remains unchanged until an approved fix is applied.

output: Extraction refused: the document appears to contain scanned images without extractable text.
The run returns exit code 2. The document is not reported as checked or clean.

output: Human review required: record the reference date for the registered claim.
Register completeness does not establish that the claim is true.

best_practices: Keep rule sources, confidence labels, and human-review recommendations attached to each finding.
Show target files and preview corrections before approving writes; review every resulting diff.
Use isolated, resource-limited processing for untrusted documents and review every extraction refusal.
anti_patterns: Treating a clean run as factual verification, legal clearance, or United Nations approval.
Automatically rewriting sensitive terminology, claims, or diplomatic language from heuristic findings.
Using watch mode in CI or relying on optional audit findings to determine the process exit code.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The portable skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code where the host can load skills and run Node.js 18 or later.

faq.question: Does it verify facts or provide United Nations approval?
faq.answer: No. It checks documented local rules and identifies review needs. It does not verify claims or represent United Nations endorsement.

faq.question: Which files can it review?
faq.answer: It reads HTML, Markdown, plain text, supported JavaScript copy, recoverable PDF text, and Word or OpenDocument body text.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my documents automatically?
faq.answer: No. Fix mode previews changes. Applying approved corrections requires an additional option and is limited to eligible Markdown and plain-text files.

faq.question: Does it retrieve pages or upload my documents?
faq.answer: It retrieves explicitly supplied HTTP(S) pages and follows redirects. The reviewed retrieval code sends no document body or environment secrets.

faq.question: What do exit codes mean?
faq.answer: Normally, 0 means no editorial errors, 1 means editorial errors, and 2 means failure. Baseline mode can accept existing errors; optional audits never fail.
